findings.reason: The two explicit translates have a useful geometric comparison: the four boundary poles of P_0 become three exterior poles and one interior pole of P_a. A faithful overlay materially clarifies why the translated contour is pole-free, independently of the complete algebraic verification.
findings.action: Added one fenced TikZ overlay and explanatory prose at the end of existing Remarks.

correction: Added the actual unit square and its translation by (1+i)/4, lattice pole dots, complex axes, boundary labels and a translation arrow; no contour orientation is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.justification: The arrow endpoints agree with the Example choice of a and the affine definition P_b=b+P_0.

diagram_math_checks.relation: All nine dots are (m,n) with m,n∈{0,1,2}; each is a double pole of wp. The four labeled dots 0,1,i,1+i lie on ∂P_0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: F1 identifies lattice coordinates; F2 and thm-weierstrass-p-normal-convergence-and-periodicity Statement clause 3 identify exactly the double poles; Verification step 1.2 identifies the four boundary poles.

diagram_math_checks.relation: No lattice dot meets ∂P_a, since its x or y coordinate is 1/4 or 5/4. The sole lattice point in its interior is (1,1), labeled 1+i; 0,1,i are outside.
